orig_text:
| One-way hash functions are commonly used to generate key identifier
| values (AKI and SKI), e.g., as described in Sections 4.1.1 and 4.1.2.
| However, none of the security properties of such functions are
| required for this context.
correct_text:
| One-way hash functions are commonly used to generate key identifier
| values (AKI and SKI), e.g., as described in Sections 4.2.1.1 and
| 4.2.1.2.  However, none of the security properties of such functions
| are required for this context.
notes:
This paragraph is added to the Security Considerations of RFC 5280, so "Sections 4.1.1 and 4.1.2" point into RFC 5280. There, Section 4.1.1 is "Certificate Fields" and Section 4.1.2 is "TBSCertificate"; neither describes key identifiers. The authority and subject key identifiers are Sections 4.2.1.1 and 4.2.1.2, and the SHA-1 methods for generating them are given in Section 4.2.1.2.
